title: iMAGING : a novel automated system for malaria diagnosis by using artificial intelligence tools and a universal low-cost robotized microscope.
summary: YOLOv5x and other object-detection CNNs were trained on 2,571 labeled thick-smear images; YOLOv5x test performance was 92.79% F-score and 94.40% mAP@0.5, and was integrated into the iMAGING microscope/app prototype. Evidence is limited to the stated retrospective/in-silico/prototype setting.
ai_technology: The learned model operation is directly used to produce the specific prediction/selection/classification finding described in the Results; this is more than generic computation or writing assistance.
organization: Microbiology Department, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Vall d'Hebron Research Institute (VHIR), Barcelona, Spain
